summary: TerraTwin is an interactive atlas for comparing Earth field locations with selected lunar and Martian research needs. It presents six candidate analog sites on a Leaflet map, grouped into Moon and Mars profiles, with research uses, NASA reference links, qualitative 1–5 fit scores, and visible weighting for terrain and geology, resource methods, environment and science, and field operations. The goal is to help teams explore where Earth field campaigns can test specific instruments and procedures before missions, while making assumptions and limitations clear. Scores are preliminary team estimates and map markers are representative points, not validated measurements or NASA ratings. Earth analogs do not reproduce lunar vacuum, low gravity or radiation, or Mars’s atmosphere and radiation. Built with React, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Python, and FastAPI, with a local JSON fallback.
details: TerraTwin compares six NASA Planetary Analog Explorer field locations with selected lunar and Mars research needs. Select a Moon or Mars profile, explore candidate sites on the Leaflet map, and open each location to review its research use, limitations, and transparent weighted fit scores. The Moon profile covers Askja volcanic terrain, Kīlauea basalt fields, and Medicine Lake lava caves. The Mars profile covers the Atacama Desert, Pilot Valley, and Death Valley. Criteria include terrain and geology, resource methods, environment and science relevance, and field operations. The scores are preliminary team judgments, not NASA ratings or validated measurements; map coordinates are representative points rather than site boundaries. Earth analogs can help teams rehearse selected instruments, sampling, traverses, and exploration procedures, but cannot reproduce lunar vacuum, low gravity, or radiation, or the Martian atmosphere and radiation. The project uses React, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Python, and FastAPI, with a local JSON fallback. ChatGPT and Codex assisted with implementation, debugging, documentation, and submission text. The team should verify all project data and claims. OpenStreetMap map tiles are attributed in the application.
